title: Soil and Waste pH
locator: Sections 3–4, interferences and apparatus. Sections 7.1–7.2, calibration and soil preparation.
summary: The soil procedure measures an aqueous phase after the specified soil-to-water mixing, settling or filtration. It describes temperature compensation, electrode selection and conditions that can bias extreme readings.
scope: Use the soil branch for soil. Report how the extract was prepared. Readings from salt solutions or a different soil-to-water ratio measure different conditions.
rights: Bibliographic record, original summary and link to the source.

title: Comparison of Soil pH Methods on Soils of North America
publisher: Soil Science Society of America Journal
version: R. O. Miller and D. E. Kissel, 74, 310–316. DOI 10.2136/sssaj2008.0047
locator: Authors’ abstract, comparison of 120 agricultural soils and the relationship with electrical conductivity.
summary: The authors compared measurements in water, salt solution and saturated paste using agricultural soils from a proficiency program. Electrical conductivity explained much of the difference between the two 1:1 water and calcium chloride pH measurements.
scope: Interpret differences in the context of the extraction liquid and soil properties. The study does not provide a universal conversion for an arbitrary soil.
rights: Bibliographic record, original summary and link to the source.

title: Standard operating procedure for soil electrical conductivity, soil/water, 1:5
locator: Sections 7–8, sample preparation, cell calibration and determination. Section 10, quality assurance and control.
summary: Measure conductivity in the soil-water extract prepared at the stated ratio. The procedure links cell calibration and temperature control to checks on duplicate samples and control material.
scope: State the extraction ratio and temperature basis. A conductivity reading on this extract cannot be substituted directly for one from saturated soil paste.
rights: Bibliographic record, original summary and link to the source.

title: Comparison of Soil EC Values from Methods Based on 1:1 and 1:5 Soil to Water Ratios and ECe from Saturated Paste Extract Based Method
locator: Sections 2.1–2.3, sampling and extraction methods. Results and discussion, comparison of extract measurements.
summary: The researchers measured extracts from soils collected in three parts of Greece. They compared soil-water ratios and agitation procedures against conductivity from saturated paste extracts.
scope: The comparison supports testing the extraction conditions for a local salinity study. Relationships derived for these soils can change with texture, salts and extract preparation.
